items.title: Periodic coloring of infinite planar graphs
items.summary: The de Bruijn–Erdős theorem states that the number of colors needed to color an infinite graph is the same as the maximum number needed for its finite subgraphs. So for any reasonable definition of an infinite planar graph, the 4-color theorem for finite planar graphs implies that every infinite planar graph is also 4-colorable.
